message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep completed for the monitored products in Products.txt, covering the last 24 hours ending with the scheduled run on 2026-06-20 05:10 IST. Confirmed relevant findings were found for Microsoft Defender, Ubuntu, and Apache Tomcat via Ubuntu packaging. A Fortinet/FortiGate credential-exposure campaign is included under possible matches because it is clearly relevant to FortiGate/FortiOS operations, but the fresh reports describe credential exposure and active abuse rather than a newly assigned CVE.

**Finding 1: Microsoft Defender RoguePlanet elevation-of-privilege vulnerability**

- Product: Windows Defender / Microsoft Defender Malware Protection Engine
- Issue: CVE-2026-50656, publicly referred to as RoguePlanet
- Severity: High, CVSS 7.8, per Microsoft/CVE reporting
- Description: Microsoft describes this as an elevation-of-privilege issue in the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine. Public reporting says the flaw can allow a local authenticated attacker to gain SYSTEM-level privileges, and Microsoft is preparing a security update.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Windows Defender, and the affected component is the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine used by Microsoft Defender.
- Source: Microsoft Security Update Guide: https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-50656; CVE record: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-50656

**Finding 2: Ubuntu / Apache Tomcat package security update**

- Product: Ubuntu and Apache Tomcat
- Issue: USN-8450-1 covering CVE-2026-41284, CVE-2026-41293, CVE-2026-42498, and CVE-2026-43515
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Ubuntu notice
- Description: Canonical fixed Tomcat issues that could allow denial of service, possible arbitrary code execution, credential exposure during WebSocket upgrades or redirects, and authorization bypass.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes both Ubuntu and Apache Tomcat; the Ubuntu notice names the tomcat11 package directly.
- Source: Ubuntu USN-8450-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8450-1

**Finding 3: Ubuntu package security notices published June 18**

- Product: Ubuntu
- Issue: USN-8454-1 libheif vulnerabilities, USN-8453-1 Net::CIDR::Lite vulnerabilities, USN-8452-1 pbkdf2 vulnerability, USN-8451-1 Vim vulnerabilities, and USN-8449-1 ldns vulnerability
- Severity: Not clearly stated in the Ubuntu notice index
- Description: Canonical published multiple package-level fixes for supported Ubuntu releases, including image-processing issues in libheif, access-control bypass risks in Net::CIDR::Lite, predictable-key risk in pbkdf2, Vim security issues, and DNS response spoofing risk in ldns.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Ubuntu, and these are official Ubuntu Security Notices published inside the review window or immediately adjacent to the scheduled run window.
- Sources: Ubuntu notices index: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices; USN-8454-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8454-1; USN-8453-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8453-1; USN-8452-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8452-1; USN-8451-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8451-1; USN-8449-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8449-1

**Possible matches needing review**

- Product: Fortigate/FortiOS / Fortinet FortiGate firewalls
- Issue: FortiBleed credential-exposure campaign; no new CVE was confirmed from the fresh sources reviewed
- Severity: Not stated as a CVSS vulnerability severity in the reviewed sources
- Description: CISA and security vendors reported exposed credentials associated with tens of thousands of Fortinet/FortiGate devices and active exploitation or abuse against internet-facing FortiGate SSL VPN infrastructure.
- Why review is needed: The monitored list includes Fortigate/FortiOS, and the affected devices are Fortinet/FortiGate firewalls. However, the fresh reports describe credential exposure and exploitation activity, not a newly disclosed vulnerability with a new CVE in the last 24 hours.
- Sources: CISA alert: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/06/18/cisa-urges-hardening-fortinet-devices-after-reports-credential-exposure; Huntress advisory: https://support.huntress.io/hc/en-us/articles/52698652545171-2026-June-Fortibleed-Credential-Exposure; IBM X-Force advisory: https://www.ibm.com/think/x-force/palo-alto-fortinet-secure-remote-access-gateway-vpn-compromise-advisory

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for Windows Defender exposure to CVE-2026-50656, Ubuntu systems running the named packages, and Ubuntu-packaged Tomcat deployments. FortiGate/FortiOS teams should also review credential hygiene and internet-facing SSL VPN exposure, but that item should be tracked as incident/exposure follow-up unless a fresh Fortinet CVE is confirmed.
